headline: Last session: Indian markets remained cautious as FPIs withdrew ₹20,974 crore amid global uncertainty and West Asia tensions.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 21 September.

why: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have withdrawn ₹20,974 crore from Indian equities in September.
Rising geopolitical tensions in West Asia and fluctuating crude oil prices are impacting investor sentiment.
The NSE grey market premium (GMP) has fallen to its lowest level since the IPO announcement.
Global market cues from Nikkei and Kospi are signaling a cautious outlook for the upcoming week.
whatHappening: A massive IPO rush is expected this week with 19 issues opening for subscription worth ₹4,169 crore.
NMDC Chairman announced a target to hit the 60 MT iron ore production mark this fiscal year.
Major corporate actions are scheduled for companies including Dixon Tech, BEML, and Titagarh Rail Systems.
NSE is set to lead the primary market activity with 12 listings scheduled for the coming days.
summary: The Indian market faces a volatile week ahead as heavy FPI selling and geopolitical risks in West Asia weigh on sentiment. Despite the macro concerns, the primary market remains hyperactive with 19 new IPOs and 12 listings led by the NSE. Investors are also tracking corporate actions in Dixon Tech and BEML alongside NMDC's ambitious production targets.
